**Why the model gave you a low‑risk decision**  
The model looks at a few key pieces of your credit profile. First, your revolving‑credit utilization is about 10 % of the available limit. Keeping balances low like this signals that you’re not over‑extending yourself, which pulls your risk down. Second, you have two open credit lines and loans. Having a modest number of accounts shows you can manage credit responsibly, further lowering the chance of default. Finally, you have no recent 30‑ to 59‑day past‑due items. The absence of these small delinquencies is another positive sign. Together, these factors lead the model to label you as “low risk” with an estimated 12.8 % probability of default, well below the threshold for higher‑risk classifications.

**How you could improve further**  
At this time, the system did not identify any feasible, constraint‑verified actions you could take that would meaningfully change the decision. Continuing the habits that earned you this low‑risk rating—keeping balances low, maintaining a manageable number of credit accounts, and avoiding late payments—will help you stay in good standing.
